claims.text: Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C.
Untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr has poor oxygen resistance that limits high-temperature use in air.
Applying an anti-oxidation coating to HfNbTaTiZr can improve its suitability for high-temperature use in air.
A thin alumina-based ceramic coating will significantly enhance the oxygen resistance of cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
The proposed alumina-based coating will remain adherent and stable during exposure at approximately 1000 °C.
The ceramic coating acts as an oxygen-diffusion barrier and reduces oxygen ingress into the alloy.
Reduced oxygen ingress limits detrimental oxide formation at the surface and in the near-surface microstructure.
Formation and penetration of oxides compromise the mechanical integrity of HfNbTaTiZr.
Slowing oxide formation and penetration will retain the bulk alloy's strength and ductility.
After exposure to air at 1000 °C for 50–100 hours, coated HfNbTaTiZr will form less oxide scale and undergo less oxidation-related degradation than uncoated material.
The coating will preserve tensile ductility relative to untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr.
The coating will preserve yield strength at 1000 °C relative to untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr.
The proposed mechanical-loading boundary at 1000 °C is a strain-rate range of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1.
The hypothesis is restricted to high-temperature exposure in air.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome can be read as placing both tensile ductility and yield strength at 1000 °C, whereas the initial state and experiment specify room-temperature ductility and yield strength at 1000 °C. The temperature at which ductility preservation is claimed is therefore inconsistent or ambiguous.
